Claire —

Thanks for the clear ask. I’ve attached an annotated draft of the Dedicated terms and a worked billing example. Short answers up front:

- Capacity unit mapping: 1 capacity unit = 4 vGPU-hours at our reference baseline (equivalent to a single p4d vGPU-hour for cost calculations). We express commits in monthly capacity units so customers can reason about predictability.

- Tiered discounts: We propose a three-slab discount schedule: 0–200k CU/month = list price; 200k–500k CU/month = 8% discount; >500k CU/month = 15% discount. Discounts apply pro-rata within the billing period.

- Ramp schedule: We’ll allow a 3-month ramp (70% month 1, 90% month 2, 100% month 3) for new commits. During ramp months pricing is aligned to committed CU for the month (i.e., discounts calculated on the committed amount, not run-rate).

- Burst/banked credits: Customers get up to 10% of committed CU as burst credits per month. Banked credits expire after 6 months and can be used across AZs within the same region.

- SLA remedies: Service credits calculated monthly. If the monthly p95 latency for committed throughput falls below the SLO, credits are X% of the monthly committed invoice per minute below SLO up to a 50% cap. We measure on an hourly aggregation window with a 7-day rolling retention for incident analysis (we can add minute-granularity logs on request).

I’ve looped in Dev to confirm the capacity mapping wording (he can call out KV cache and batching effects) and Marissa for the worked example and the DocuSign link.

Next steps: if the wording looks acceptable, we can take your redlines in DocuSign and route to our legal team. Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Rachel

Claire / Rachel — quick technical clarification to include in the annotated terms so procurement has no surprises:

- Definition detail: 1 capacity unit (CU) = 4 vGPU-hours at our baseline performance profile (baseline = fp16, no KV-cache warming, 1k token context). For customers using larger context or different quantization, we provide an effective CU conversion table (example in docx).

- KV cache & batching: Effective CU consumption is sensitive to workload profile: persistent KV cache utilization reduces per-request GPU work and therefore the effective CU burn rate. We’ll publish a normalized conversion example: e.g., Chat workload with warm KV cache and batching factor 8 -> ~0.7x CU burn vs stateless single-token workloads. That conversion is advisory for billing examples, not an automated meter unless agreed in the SOW.

- Measurement windows: SLA uses a blended hourly aggregation for throughput/latency SLOs and a daily availability check for capacity availability. Service credit triggers on hourly aggregates; per-minute samples are retained for forensics but not for credit calc (avoids minute spikes creating volatility).

I’ll add those lines into the draft and flag the sections where the legal team might want tighter language.

—Dev

Hi Claire — attaching a worked billing example using your capacity_estimate_medtech.xlsx (tab: "May-Jun projection"). Key notes in the sheet:

- Example conversion: 100k vGPU-hours (projected) -> 25k CUs (at 4 vGPU-hours per CU).
- Billing example: Month 1 run-rate 20k CU, committed 25k CU -> you pay committed price for 25k CU less ramp discount (70% month 1), overage billed at list but eligible for burst credits first.
- Discount application: pro-rata within month; if you consume 30k CU but commit 25k CU with tier crossing, the extra 5k is billed at the tiered rate corresponding to that tranche (see sheet rows 42-48).

SLA credit calc (sheet notes): monthly service credit = min(50%, round((SLO_shortfall_minutes / total_billed_minutes) * committed_monthly_invoice, 2)). We included a sample calculation assuming 120 shortfall minutes. Legal may prefer percent-of-monthly-invoice instead; we can swap formulas.

Questions for you:
- Do you need the CU conversion locked in the contract or can we include it as an annex (recommended so we can adjust per-model/per-context)?
- For banked credits, is 6-month expiry acceptable? We can extend to 12 months at a different discount tier.

If this model looks reasonable I’ll prepare a tracked-changes docx for your legal team.

Cheers,

Thanks all — this is very helpful. Procurement and legal reviewed the example and have a few requested redlines (summary):

1) Capacity unit mapping: request that the CU->vGPU-hour table be embedded in the contract (not just an annex). They want an explicit conversion table with a clause that any future re-baselining requires 90 days notice.
2) Ramp & termination: they want the ramp to be optional by customer (i.e., if we miss month 1 they can reduce the committed amount without penalty within a 30-day window).
3) SLA measurement: they prefer minute-granularity for credits to better reflect clinical availability.
4) Banked credits: ask to extend expiry to 12 months and allow cross-region use for hybrid deployments.

They provided inline comments in DocuSign (link above) and asked for a tracked-change doc. Can you review and let me know items you expect negotiation on vs. those you can accept? We need legal to issue PO by 2027-05-10.

Claire — thanks for the quick review and the DocuSign comments. We reviewed internally and here’s what we can commit to and what will require a brief legal discussion:

Acceptable with minor edits:
- Banked credits expiry extended to 12 months (we’ll add a cap to total banked balance equal to 20% of annual committed CU).
- Cross-AZ burst usage within a region — acceptable. Cross-region banked credit use will require a premium.

Requires legal discussion / negotiation:
- Embedding the CU->vGPU conversion table in the main contract (we prefer it in an annex to allow model/quant changes; we can add a 90-day notice baseline change clause).
- Minute-granularity for SLA credits (we currently calculate credits on hourly aggregates to avoid volatility). We can include minute-level logs for audit and negotiate a blended approach (hourly calc + minute-level evidence for escalations).
- Ramp opt-out: we can offer a one-time ramp flexibility for year-1 with a 30-day window; permanent opt-out will affect pricing/discounts.
